options: Any repeated text anywhere in the prompt
A byte-identical prefix of the prompt seen recently
explanation: Only a prefix can be reused; the first variable part ends it.

options: System prompt, tool schemas, examples first; retrieved context next; the user's turn last
explanation: Stable first, variable last maximises the identical prefix.

stem: A date at the start of the system prompt…
options: Breaks the cacheable prefix every day (or every request)
explanation: Anything variable before the stable parts ends the cacheable prefix there.

stem: Cached input is typically billed at…
options: A fraction (often ~10%) of the normal input price
explanation: That is why a large stable prefix with a high hit rate changes the bill materially.

stem: How do you know caching is working?
options: Read the cached vs uncached input token counts the API returns and track the hit rate
explanation: Put the hit rate on a dashboard; a drop means someone edited the prefix.

options: Work nobody is waiting for — nightly jobs, backfills, evals, re-indexing — at a discount
explanation: Same work, lower price, minutes-to-hours latency.

stem: Reordering a prompt for caching changes…
options: The bill — not the answers or the model
explanation: It is a refactor with a measurable saving and often better latency (prompt processing skipped).

stem: Why might a short stable prefix not be cached?
options: It is cached but not billed
Providers have a minimum cacheable length
Caching is only for system prompts
explanation: Check the provider's rules; they differ and change.

stem: Per-request tool lists in the system section…
options: Make the 'stable' prefix variable and defeat caching — keep tool lists constant per route
explanation: Anything that changes per request must come after the stable prefix.

stem: What fraction of a typical product's model calls can go to batch?
options: Often a third or more — reports, nightly classification, evals, re-embedding
explanation: The trick is noticing which calls nobody is waiting for.
